item.title: On condensations of $C_p(X)$ spaces onto Banach spaces with the weak topology
item.description: arXiv:2610.24165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that for a broad class of spaces $X$, the space $C_p(X)$ of continuous real-valued functions on $X$ equipped with the pointwise topology maps bijectively onto any separable infinite-dimensional Banach space with the weak topology. We prove that the inverse $\varphi^{-1}$ of any continuous bijection $\varphi: C_p(X)\to (E,w)$, where $X$ is an arbitrary infinite Tychonoff space and $(E,w)$ is an arbitrary normed space with the weak topology, is everywhere discontinuous. This generalizes a recent result of Kania--K\k{a}kol and solves a problem raised by K\k{a}kol, Leiderman and Michalak by providing a complete classification of function spaces $C_p(X)$ that are homeomorphic to Banach spaces with the weak topology.
item.dc:creator: Miko\l aj Krupski, Witold Marciszewski

item.title: Two-parameter Toeplitz-type operators between Fock spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.24318v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce and study a two-parameter family of Toeplitz-type operators $T^{(s,t)}_\varphi$ on the Fock space $F^p(C)$ for $0<p\leq\infty$. For all $0<p, q \leq\infty$ we obtain sharp conditions for $\varphi$ such that $T^{(s,t)}_\varphi: F^p(C)\to F^q(C)$ is bounded or compact. In the Hilbert space case $T^{(s,t)}_\varphi: F^2(C)\to F^2(C)$, we also study the Berezin transform of $T^{(s,t)}_\varphi$ and membership of $T^{(s,t)}_\varphi$ in Schatten classes. Furthermore, we find a class of noncompact operators whose Berezin transforms nevertheless vanish at infinity.
item.dc:creator: Xingtang Dong, Zipeng Wang, Kehe Zhu

item.title: Minimality of $T_z^*$-Invariant Subspaces of $H^2(\mathbb D^2)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.24327v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish necessary conditions for the minimality of infinite-dimensional $T_z^*$-invariant subspaces of $H^2(\mathbb D^2)$. More precisely, we prove that if $M\subset H^2(\mathbb D^2)$ is an infinite-dimensional, minimal $T_z^*$-invariant subspace, then, for every $n\in\mathbb N_0$, either $\overline{P_n(M)}=H^2(\mathbb D)$ or $\overline{P_n(M)}^\perp =\phi_{a,\theta}H^2(\mathbb D)$ where $\phi_{a,\theta}$ is an atomic singular inner function and $P_n$ denotes the orthogonal projection of $H^2(\mathbb D^2)$ onto $H^2(z)w^n$. As $T_z^*$ is a universal operator on $H^2(\mathbb D^2)$, this result reduces the Invariant Subspace Problem to the analysis of these two alternatives for infinite-dimensional minimal $T_z^*$-invariant subspaces.
item.dc:creator: Jo\~ao Marcos R. do Carmo, Marcos S. Ferreira

item.title: Certified Fourier rounding for the real Grothendieck inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.24417v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof that the real Grothendieck constant is strictly smaller than $1.77987164$. The proof provides a complete interval-arithmetic realization of Ren's five-variable construction. A finite Fourier calculation encloses every scalar coefficient through degree $403$; a fourth-derivative estimate on the entire unit circle bounds the remaining coefficient sum by $10^{-4}$. Exact rational arithmetic then certifies the final inequality. We include the transfer to all finite real matrices and arbitrary vector dimensions, the analytic quadrature errors, the rational parameters, and source code for checking and regenerating the certificate.
item.dc:creator: Bo Peng

item.title: Zero-trace index of matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.24486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The zero-trace index $t(A)$ of a square complex matrix $A$ is introduced. It is defined as the largest integer $k$ such that $A$ admits a $k \times k$ compression with trace zero. This concept is analogous to the zero-dilation index $d(A)$ and is closely related to the $k$-numerical range. The $k$-numerical range is characterized as an intersection of half-planes, which is used to derive a formula for $t(A)$ that reduces its computation to the Hermitian case. Conditions for $t(A) = d(A)$ are also established, and matrices satisfying $t(A) = n - 1$ are characterized. Finally, the zero-trace index is determined for several classes of matrices.
item.dc:creator: Kennett L. Dela Rosa, Eloise P. Misa

item.title: Extension of surjective isometries between unit spheres of $\ell^p$-direct sums
item.description: arXiv:2610.24533v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study surjective isometries between the unit spheres of Banach spaces of the form $A\oplus_p B$, where $A$ is nonzero and strictly convex, $1<p<\infty$, and every unit vector of $B\neq\{0\}$ has at least two distinct unit vectors at distance $2$. For two direct sums $A_i\oplus_{p_i}B_i$, $i=1,2$, satisfying these hypotheses, we prove that every surjective isometry $$\Delta:S_{A_1\oplus_{p_1}B_1}\to S_{A_2\oplus_{p_2} B_2}$$ between their unit spheres forces equality of the direct-sum exponents $p_i$ and extends uniquely to a surjective real-linear isometry $$\widetilde{\Delta}:A_1\oplus_p B_1\to A_2\oplus_p B_2$$ preserving the corresponding components, where $p:=p_1=p_2$. The proof identifies the component unit spheres through diametral sets and distance formulas, and then constructs isometries between the component unit balls. As a principal application, we obtain extension and representation results for absolutely continuous functions equipped with norms combining evaluation at a fixed point and the $L^1$-norm of the derivative. We also discuss Lipschitz and differentiable function spaces, distinguishing the consequences of our theorem from those already covered by existing extension results. Endpoint conclusions are derived separately, including the Mazur-Ulam property for the real absolutely continuous space with the sum norm.
item.dc:creator: Min-Ruei Lin

item.title: Commutative exact superalgebras and super-modular tensor categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.24568v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the theory of commutative exact algebras in braided finite tensor categories (Shimizu-Yadav) to superalgebras, motivated by extensions of vertex operator (super)algebras. For a braided category $\C$ let $\B=\C^{\gr}$ be the category of $\mathbb Z/2$-graded objects with the Koszul-signed braiding. It is the underlying category of the supercategory of Creutzig-Kanade-McRae. A supercommutative superalgebra $A=A_0\oplus A_1$ in $\C$ is the same as a commutative algebra $\bA$ in $\B$, and super-local modules are the local $\bA$-modules. Hence rigidity, pivotality and ribbon statements are instances of the ordinary theorems, with the ribbon condition $\theta_{A_0}=\id$, $\theta_{A_1}=\varepsilon\,\id$, where $\varepsilon=\pm1$ is fixed by the statistics of the odd part. For $\C$ non-degenerate and $\bA$ haploid and exact we prove that the category of super-local modules is a braided finite tensor category whose M\"uger center is $\mathsf{sVect}$. It is the centralizer of a fermion in a non-degenerate category obtained by condensing in $\C\boxtimes(\text{toric code})$. If $\C$ is ribbon and $\bA$ is symmetric Frobenius it is ribbon. We construct examples from graded simple currents, treat the free fermion and the symplectic fermion, and compare with Creutzig-Kanade-McRae and Creutzig-McRae-Shimizu-Yadav.
item.dc:creator: A. Zuevsky

item.title: Complex Representatives, Similarity Invariants, and Iterates in $\bf{U(1,1;\mathbb{H})}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.24580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the similarity classes of matrices in $U(1,1;\mathbb H)$ and the iterates of their associated quaternionic M\"obius transformations. Building on the known elliptic case, we show that every parabolic or loxodromic element of $U(1,1;\mathbb H)$ is similar, via a matrix in $U(1,1;\mathbb H)$, to a complex matrix. Explicit complex representatives and matrices realizing these similarities are constructed for the different types. We then introduce the invariants $\operatorname{Tr}(T), \Delta(T), \eta(T), \kappa(T)$, and prove that they form a complete system of similarity invariants for matrices in $U(1,1;\mathbb H)$. Finally, using the complex representation of quaternionic matrices and Chebyshev polynomials, we derive a fourth-order recurrence for a real sequence $(q_n)$ satisfying $\Delta(T^n)=q_n^2\Delta(T)$. Together with recurrence relations for the relevant matrix entries, this identity yields a complete classification of the quaternionic M\"obius transformation associated with $T^n$, including the degenerate cases in which $\Delta(T^n)=0$.
item.dc:creator: Bingzhe Hou, Cailing Yao, Jiaxing He

item.title: Locally convex spaces with hemicompact weak* dual
item.description: arXiv:2610.24615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a locally convex space $L$ let $L'_\sigma$ denote its dual endowed with the weak* topology $\sigma(L',L)$. We prove that $L'_\sigma$ is hemicompact if and only if $L$ with the Mackey topology $\tau(L,L')$ is metrizable and barrelled, and if and only if $L'_\sigma$ is $\sigma$-compact and quasi-complete. The key step is that a hemicompact $L'_\sigma$ is quasi-complete. The Mackey topology $\tau(L,L')$ is metrizable if and only if $L'$ is a countable union of absolutely convex weak*-compact sets; spaces with normable barrelled Mackey topology are characterized similarly. As a consequence, a metrizable (in particular, normed) space $L$ is barrelled if and only if $L'_\sigma$ is hemicompact. For function spaces we obtain: $(C_k(X))'_\sigma$ is hemicompact if and only if $X$ is hemicompact, and $(C_p(X))'_\sigma$ is hemicompact if and only if $X$ is countable and all compact subsets of $X$ are finite.
item.dc:creator: Evgenii Reznichenko

item.title: Weighted Power Means on Upper Triangular Matrix Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.24821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study weighted power means on the Lie group $\operatorname{UT}_n$ of real upper triangular matrices with positive diagonal entries. For $t\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, the weighted power mean $P_t(\mathbf{w}; A_1,\ldots,A_m)$ is defined by \[ X=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i(X\#_tA_i), \qquad X\#_tA:=X(X^{-1}A)^t. \] Using divided differences, analytic matrix functions, and the Parlett recurrence, we prove existence, uniqueness, and real-analytic dependence of $P_t$ on the data and the weights. We derive finite entrywise and block-recursive algorithms, establish structural properties of the mean, and obtain explicit formulas for the cases $\operatorname{UT}_2$ and $\operatorname{UT}_3$. We prove that $P_t$ converges to the weighted Karcher mean as $t\to 0$. We also establish a Lie--Trotter formula and derive second-order asymptotic expansions for the power, Karcher, and log-Euclidean means, showing that the parameter $t$ first enters the local behavior at second order.
item.dc:creator: Huajun Huang

item.title: Operators commuting with $L^\infty$]{Operators commuting with $L^\infty$ on K\"othe--Bochner spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.24853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $E(X)$ be a K\"othe--Bochner space of functions on a $\sigma$-finite measure space with values in a Banach space $X$. We study bounded operators on $E(X)$ that commute with the operators of multiplication by functions from $L^\infty$. If $X$ is separable, every such operator acts pointwise by an essentially bounded $L(X)$-valued function. For a nonseparable $X$, a lifting of $L^\infty$ provides a representation by $L(X,X^{\star\star})$-valued functions, and by $L(X)$-valued functions if $X$ is complemented in $X^{\star\star}$, with the sharp norm bound if $X$ is a dual space. As an application, we show that if the transformation is aperiodic, then the spectral projections of invertible weighted composition operators with operator-valued weights are operators of multiplication by $L(X)$-valued functions whenever $X$ is separable or complemented in $X^{\star\star}$, and that, if moreover the measure is ergodic and $\dim X = m < \infty$, the spectrum of such an operator has at most $m$ connected components. Finally, for $L^p(\mu;X)$, $1 \leq p < \infty$, an aperiodic nonsingular transformation and a weight that is measurable in the operator norm, we prove that the spectral projections are operators of multiplication by projection-valued functions for an arbitrary Banach space $X$, for instance for $X = c_0(\Gamma)$ with $\Gamma$ uncountable. The proof uses an inverse-closedness result for the algebra generated by norm-measurable multipliers and the composition operator.
item.dc:creator: Hulya Duru, Serkan Ilter, Arkady Kitover, Mehmet Orhon

item.title: Opposed Exponent Profiles and Real Interpolation of Measurable Subspaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.24904v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study real interpolation of the $G$-measurable subspaces $Y_j$ of variable Lebesgue spaces $L^{p_j(\cdot)}$. For a family of continuous exponent pairs that vary in opposite directions on the atoms of $G$, we prove that $K$-closedness is equivalent to a uniform logarithmic bound on the oscillation of the exponents. The same bound characterizes the existence of a common bounded projection and interpolation equality at a single interior parameter. If it fails, then for each $0<\theta<1$ there is one function belonging to all ambient interpolation spaces $(X_0,X_1)_{\theta,q}$, $0<q\leq\infty$, and to none of the corresponding spaces $(Y_0,Y_1)_{\theta,q}$. Each endpoint subspace still admits a bounded positive projection. The exponents can be chosen arbitrarily close to prescribed constants $1<a<b<\infty$, with constant sum and smoothness away from zero. We also give a finite-profile criterion in terms of the endpoint maxima, compute the associated $K$-functional loss, and obtain a counterexample for adapted sequence spaces.
item.dc:creator: Asad Ullah

item.title: Local Nevanlinna embedding for Hardy space of Dirichlet series below critical exponent
item.description: arXiv:2610.25002v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate a problem posed by Saksman and Seip [ Contemp. Math., 2016] on whether functions in the Hardy space of Dirichlet series $\mathcal{H}^p$, \(0<p<2\), are locally in the Nevanlinna class of the critical half-plane \(\mathbb C_{1/2}\). We show that the local Nevanlinna embedding fails below critical exponent \(p=2\) by constructing $\mathcal{H}^p$-functions whose local logarithmic mass becomes unbounded as \(\real s\to 1/2^+\). This also clarifies the distinction between global Jessen-type logarithmic control and local boundary Nevanlinna behavior for Dirichlet series.
item.dc:creator: Vasudevarao Allu, Dipon Kumar Mondal

item.title: On an open question about the equivalence of monotone maximality and surjectivity condition in $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ spaces: Negative and partially positive answers
item.description: arXiv:2610.25080v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a Hilbert space, it is known that a monotone operator is maximal if and only if the \emph{surjectivity condition}, \ie its resolvent has a full domain, holds. This equivalence is an open question in a $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ space, knowing only that the surjectivity condition implies the monotone maximality. In fact, there have been three approaches to generalize the monotonicity from a Hilbert space into a $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ space $X$ --- \textbf{A:} the ones of dual space $X^{\ast}$, \textbf{B:} of linear dual space $X^{\diamond}$, and \textbf{C:} of tangent bundle $TX$. In this paper, we answer \emph{negatively} on the first two approaches by constructing counterexamples on an $\mathbb{R}$-tree. We then go on proving that the equivalence is \emph{affirmative} on the same $\mathbb{R}$-tree, without any assumption on the domain. Moreover, we show that the answer is still \emph{positive} in some other cases, through a flat slice principle that transfers Minty's principle from Hilbert spaces to flat convex subsets, and through Minty's principle on proper Hilbert-Hadamard spaces satisfying a convex half-space condition. The question of equivalence \emph{remains open} under the general setting with the tangential approach.
item.dc:creator: Parin Chaipunya

item.title: Boundedness of nonregular bilinear pseudodifferential operators on variable Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.25234v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we introduce two bilinear, non-regular symbol classes\linebreak $BS\mathcal B^m_\delta(r,\mu,v;N,\lambda)$ and $BS\mathcal F^m_\delta(r,\mu,v;N,\lambda)$, where $m\in\mathbb R$, $0\leq\delta<1$, $0<\mu,v\leq\infty$, $1\leq\lambda\leq2$, $r>n/\mu$, and $N>2n/\lambda$, with $\mu<\infty$ for the latter class. For $\mu\geq1$, $(1-\delta)r\geq n/\mu$, and sufficiently large $N$, we establish boundedness of the associated bilinear pseudodifferential operators on Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces with variable smoothness, integrability and summation exponents. To the best of the authors' knowledge, these operator estimates are new even on the classical Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces with constant exponents. As an application, we establish the multiplication algebra property for both variable exponent spaces.
item.dc:creator: Tengfei Bai, Jingshi Xu, Jinlai Zhu

item.title: Geometric and measure-theoretic characterizations of the measure-determining property of balls in metric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.25698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The question of what structural properties drive the collection of open or closed balls to uniquely determine Borel probability measures on a metric space, the ball property, has a long history in measure theory. While various sufficient conditions have been known since the 1970s, and it was shown by Preiss and Ti\v{s}er (1991) that it holds for all separable Banach spaces, Davies (1971) constructed a famous counterexample that shows it can fail on compact metric spaces. It was only recently established in van Delft (2026) that metric spaces admitting an isometric Hilbertian embedding must possess the ball property. This article provides a comprehensive structural and measure-theoretic characterization of the ball property. First, we establish a necessary and sufficient condition for the ball property to fail: the collection of balls must possess sufficient combinatorial capacity, which we define as charged dyadic shattering. Second, by characterizing the ball property via $\lambda$-systems, we place classical vector space results within a unified context. Building on this to understand spaces that have the topological capacity but lack linear or geometric rigidity required to force ball-annihilating measures to zero, we relate the metric outer measure to the cylinder outer measure on countable products of Polish spaces, deriving necessary and sufficient measure-theoretic conditions for the ball property to hold. This allows us to derive a structural taxonomy on the decoupling of the metric outer measure from the cylinder outer measure. This is subsequently used to deconstruct Davies' counterexample. Finally, we introduce a minimal combinatorial generalization of the ball property, the $n$th order ball property, and show that such classes can fully recover measure determination in highly pathological constructions like Davies' counterexample.
item.dc:creator: Anne van Delft

item.title: Noncommutative maximal weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for convolution operators under $L_1$-H\"ormander conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.25761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for families of scalar convolution operators acting on operator-valued function spaces. A joint $L_1$-H\"ormander condition, together with a maximal strong type estimate at one exponent $1<r\leq\infty$, suffices. The kernels may be complex-valued and need not have uniformly bounded $L_1$ norms. Under a size condition, the result also yields a weak endpoint estimate for all sharp truncation radii of singular kernels. This resolves, for convolution kernels, the problem mentioned in \cite[Remark~5.5]{parcet09pseudo} and recalled in Parcet's recent survey \cite[Remark~1.3]{Parcet2026ICM}. The proof involves not only a simultaneous dyadic representation of the operators but also a noncommutative maximal weak type $(1,1)$ estimates of the resulting dyadic operators. This approach seems entirely new even in the commutative setting. Numerous applications are provided. On the one hand, it yields various maximal inequalities and pointwise convergence results for integrable kernels and dyadic approximations of the identity, monotone $L\log L$ majorants, and Poisson integrals on nilpotent groups and symmetric spaces. On the other hand, via various transference techniques, it implies maximal inequalities for Fourier multipliers, Schur multipliers and double operator integrals, together with bilateral almost uniform convergence of dyadic Fourier summation methods on $L_1$ of group von Neumann algebras.
item.dc:creator: Guixiang Hong, Liang Wang, Xumin Wang, Bang Xu

item.title: Approximation numbers of critical Besov embeddings
item.description: arXiv:2610.25910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the approximation numbers of critical embeddings between isotropic Besov spaces on nonempty bounded Lipschitz domains in any dimension. For 0 < p_1 < 2 < p_2 <= infinity and s_1 - s_2 = d max{1/p_1, 1 - 1/p_2} > d(1/p_1 - 1/p_2), the approximation numbers have order N^{-1/2}(log(e+N))^Gamma for every 0 < q_1, q_2 <= infinity, with an explicit four-case formula for Gamma. This resolves the strictly compact critical Besov approximation-number problem identified in Vybiral's overview. For q_1 < q_2, the logarithmic exponent depends on the ordering of p_1' and p_2; it can vanish for one pair (p_1,p_2) and remain positive for another with the same fine indices. A row estimate for the approximation error gives lower bounds when the target fine index is below one. Gaussian finite-rank approximations acting on several levels give the sharp upper bounds when Gamma < 1/2. For q_1 < q_2, matching lower bounds for the two strict orderings of the inner indices follow from Malykhin's finite-window estimates and norm comparisons. The results include quasi-Banach indices and the full spaces of bounded coefficient sequences at infinite fine indices.
item.dc:creator: Feng Guo

item.title: Compactness and weak compactness of linearized Holomorphic-Lipschitz maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.26047v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Any holomorphic Lipschitz map $f$, defined on the open unit ball $B_X$ of a complex Banach space $X$ and taking values in a complex Banach space $Y$, can be uniquely and canonically associated with a bounded linear operator $\widehat f : \mathcal G_0(B_X) \longrightarrow \mathcal G_0(Y)$ between the corresponding holomorphic Lipschitz-free spaces. The aim of this paper is to establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the compactness and weak compactness of such operators. In particular, we obtain a general characterisation of the compactness of $\widehat f$ in terms of metric properties of its symbol $f$. We then focus on the case where the target space is a subspace of $\ell_p$, $1\leq p<\infty$. When the target space is $\ell_1$, we show that compactness and weak compactness of $\widehat f$ are both equivalent to $\widehat f$ not fixing a copy of $\ell_1$. Finally, when the target space is $\ell_p$ with $1<p<\infty$, we obtain a metric characterisation of the weak compactness of $\widehat f$. As a consequence, we show that compactness and weak compactness need not coincide, even when the target space is $\ell_p$.
item.dc:creator: Fr\'ed\'eric Bayart, Mathis Lemay, Colin Petitjean

item.title: Zero products of Toeplitz operators with harmonic symbols on the Bergman space of the unit ball
item.description: arXiv:2610.26139v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, using local boundary factorizations of harmonic functions and singular-value estimates for Toeplitz products, we study the zero-product problem for Toeplitz operators on the Bergman space of the unit ball in $\mathbb{C}^n$. We prove that a finite product of such operators is zero only if one of the symbols is identically zero, provided that all the symbols are harmonic on the open unit ball and continuous on the closed unit ball.
item.dc:creator: Jiawei Wang, Xianfeng Zhao

item.title: Prescribed Beurling densities in spectral eigen-subspaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.26146v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(q,D,L)$ be a one-dimensional Hadamard triple with $2\leq m:=\#D<q$, and let $\mu_{q,D}$ be the associated self-similar probability measure. Write $\mathcal T=\{t\in\mathbb Z:(q,D,tL)\text{ is a Hadamard triple}\}$. We prove that, for every $0<s<\log m/\log q$ and every $\zeta\in[0,+\infty]$, there are continuum many spectra $\Lambda$ of $\mu_{q,D}$ such that $t\Lambda$ is a spectrum for every $t\in\mathcal T$, $\dim_{\mathrm{Be}}\Lambda=s$, and $D_s^+(\Lambda)=\zeta$. The construction combines a nested family of finite digit sets with lacunary spectral extensions. A two-sided interval-counting estimate controls the density of the prescribed subset, while the added frequencies ensure completeness for every multiplier without changing that density. Binary choices in the extension yield continuum many distinct spectra. This refines Beurling dimension interpolation in spectral eigen-subspaces by prescribing the upper density at every strictly intermediate dimension.
item.dc:creator: Zheng-Yi Lu

item.title: A proof of the Baranov--Bessonov--Kapustin conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.26232v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the conjecture of Baranov, Bessonov and Kapustin: for a non-constant inner function $\theta$, every bounded truncated Toeplitz operator on the model space $K_\theta$ has a bounded symbol if and only if $\theta$ is one-component
item.dc:creator: Carlo Bellavita, Jani A. Virtanen

item.title: Two pointwise estimates for singular integral operators over p-adic groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.26248v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish some new pointwise boundedness properties for rough singular integral operators defined over p-adic groups. The properties of these operator rely essentially on the behavior of their rough kernels and we will present two different cases that fall outside the setting of the classical Calder{\'o}n-Zygmund setting.
item.dc:creator: Diego Chamorro (LaMME)

item.title: Semigroup of composition operators on the Fock space of several complex variables
item.description: arXiv:2610.26349v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper considers discrete and continuous semigroups of composition operators on the Fock space of several complex variables. For discrete semigroups generated by a single operator, the asymptotic behaviour is analysed. Strongly continuous semigroups are studied, and in particular it is shown that the classical Berkson-Porta theorem fails in this context. As an application, we show that any bounded composition operator is strongly reducible on the Fock space and that it is mean-ergodic.
item.dc:creator: Fr{\'e}d{\'e}ric Bayart (LMBP), Maofa Wang, Xingxing Yao

item.title: Triebel - Lizorkin spaces of dominating mixed smoothness are algebras with respect to pointwise multiplication
item.description: arXiv:2610.26415v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We continue our investigations on pointwise multipliers for spaces of dominating mixed smoothness. In this paper we prove that under a certain conditions Triebel - Lizorkin spaces of dominating mixed smoothness form algebras with respect to pointwise multiplication.
item.dc:creator: Van Kien Nguyen

item.title: Limits of Besov Norms on Quantum Euclidean Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.26463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the Bourgain--Br\'{e}zis--Mironescu (BBM) and Maz'ya--Shaposhnikova (MS) limit formulae to higher-order Besov norms on quantum Euclidean spaces $\R^d_\theta$, a fundamental class of noncompact noncommutative manifolds obtained by deformation quantization of $\R^d$. A central ingredient is a Banach realization of the homogeneous Sobolev endpoint that forms a compatible couple with \(L_p(\R_\theta^d)\), together with the equivalence \[ K\bigl(\x,\varepsilon^k; L_p(\R_\theta^d),\dot W_{p,0}^k(\R_\theta^d)\bigr) \approx \omega_p^k(\x,\varepsilon). \] This framework yields a unified proof of both endpoint formulae through the endpoint continuity of real interpolation scales. The principal new ingredient at the MS endpoint is the sharp large-translation asymptotic \[ \lim_{|h|\to\infty}\|T_h\x-\x\|_p = 2^{1/p}\|\x\|_p, \qquad \x\in L_p(\R_\theta^d),\quad 1\leq p<\infty, \] whose proof combines oscillatory decay of the non-pure terms in the tracial expansion with weighted spectral-measure arguments adapted to the semifinite trace.
item.dc:creator: Qingquan Deng, Guixiang Hong, Ping Li, Yanzhen Long

item.title: Powers and Functional Calculus for $m$-Selfadjoint and Skew $m$-Selfadjoint Operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.26572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study powers and functional calculi of higher-order selfadjoint and skew higher-order selfadjoint operators on complex Hilbert spaces. First, we compare the behavior of their powers with the corresponding theory for $m$-isometries. We prove that if $T$ is invertible and two powers $T^r$ and $T^s$ are, respectively, $m$- and $\ell$-selfadjoint, then $T^{\gcd(r,s)}$ is $\min\{m,\ell\}$-selfadjoint. In particular, invertibility yields the expected converse for consecutive powers. We also show that two consecutive skew $m$-selfadjoint powers must be non-invertible; in fact, nilpotent. For polynomials, we obtain coefficient characterizations under a cardinality assumption on the spectrum. Finally, for holomorphic functions we give spectral characterizations according to whether the spectrum is finite, or the domain of analyticity is a region, and we derive consequences for M\"obius transformations and $m$-isometries. Several examples illustrate why the spectral hypotheses cannot be omitted.
item.dc:creator: M. Faghih-Ahmadi, T. Berm\'udez, K. Hedayatian, H. Zaway

item.title: On the uniqueness of $p$-energy on the Sierpi\'nski carpet
item.description: arXiv:2610.26720v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For any $p\in(1,+\infty)$, it is proved that the self-similar $p$-energy on the Sierpi\'nski carpet is unique, up to multiplication by a positive constant.
item.dc:creator: Meng Yang

item.title: A two-dimensional subspace of $\ell_\infty^3$ has a unique operator space structure if and only if it is isometric to $\ell_\infty^2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.26738v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that a two-dimensional complex subspace of $\ell_\infty^3$ carries a unique operator space structure if and only if it is isometric to $\ell_\infty^2$; the ``if'' half is the And\^o's theorem. For each of the remaining spaces we exhibit an explicit non-normal $Y \in \mathcal{M}_2$, with $(I,Y)$ an extreme point of the associated matrix ball, for which the induced linear map is contractive but not completely contractive. Since every two-dimensional subspace of $\ell_\infty^3$ has the $2$-summing property, the $2$-summing property does not imply uniqueness of the operator space structure for two dimensional complex Banach spaces.
item.dc:creator: Rajeev Gupta, Arpita Mal, Gadadhar Misra, Samya Kumar Ray

item.title: Functional Model for Isometric Pairs Satisfying an Automorphic Covariance Relation - I
item.description: arXiv:2610.26773v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive a canonical functional model for a pair of isometric operators $(V_1, V_2)$ acting on a Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ that satisfy the automorphic covariance relation $V_1 V_2 = V_2 \varphi(V_1)$, where $\varphi$ is an automorphism of the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$. This extends the classical Bercovici--Douglas--Foias functional model for commuting isometric pairs to a dynamically twisted setting. When both $V_1$ and $V_2$ are pure isometries (shifts), the model simplifies to $(M_z, M_{\Theta} W_\varphi^*)$ acting on $H^2(\mathcal{F})$, where $W_\varphi$ is a unitary weighted composition operator on the Hardy space $H^2$ and $\Theta \in H^\infty(\mathbb{D}, \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{F}))$ is an operator-valued inner function such that $M_{\Theta}$ is a shift. As an application, we establish a complete unitary classification theorem for automorphically covariant isometric pairs by identifying a complete set of joint unitary invariants. Notably, our results are novel even in the special case of rotation automorphisms ($V_1 V_2 = q V_2 V_1$ with $|q| = 1$).
item.dc:creator: Sourav Ghosh, Haripada Sau

item.title: Muckenhoupt weights for the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator on hyperbolic spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.26818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On the real hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^n$, the classical Muckenhoupt condition does not describe the weights $w$ for which the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator $M$ is bounded on $L^p(w)$. We show that, for $1<p<\infty$, $M$ is bounded on $L^p(w)$ if and only if $w$ is a local $A_p$ weight and satisfies a two-layer condition, which compares $w$ and its dual weight on two layers of the shadow of a point. We also treat the weak type case, radial weights and the range $p\le1$, and we prove a weighted Herz principle for radial convolution operators.
item.dc:creator: Tapendu Rana

item.title: Mathematics of Herding
item.description: arXiv:2610.23992v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A herd of animals often follows a leader who sets the direction of travel. The leader sometimes turns unexpectedly and the followers reshuffle. Yet the herd regroups itself and stays coherent. Our work aims to understand the herding behavior mathematically. We construct a minimal discrete-time nonequilibrium dynamical system with one-way coupling, and the minimal structure allows an exact analysis. Take the location of each follower in the frame of the leader. The recorded locations form a distribution. The limit of the distribution is the asymptotic spatial measure, whose geometric representation we study. The dynamics of the herd have an exact operator representation with two factors, the operator of a fixed leader-follower pair and the operator of the interaction rules, which reshuffle the pairs. We show that the influence of the leader passes through some follower more than once. As a result, two followers can have reciprocal influence, despite the one-way coupling.
item.dc:creator: Sayomi Kamimoto

item.title: A Pricing and Hedging Framework for Infinite-Dimensional Financial Markets
item.description: arXiv:2610.24169v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we provide a comprehensive study of how the classical Black--Scholes-type market framework behaves in an infinite-dimensional setting. The asset prices are modeled by stochastic evolution equations in a separable Hilbert space. The evolution of the risk-free asset and the corresponding discounting operators are governed by a strongly continuous group of bounded linear operators. Accordingly, we consider contingent claims with Hilbert-space-valued payoffs, whose values are discounted through the corresponding operators. Within this framework, we investigate the pricing and hedging of contingent claims, deriving the corresponding infinite-dimensional Black--Scholes equations and establishing exact replication results for strong solutions and asymptotic replication results for mild solutions through Yosida approximations. We also study the special case where the infinitesimal generator is given by $A=rI$, allowing for real-valued contingent claims. We further investigate no-arbitrage and market completeness, introducing a Hilbert lattice structure to formulate arbitrage and characterizing attainability through operator equations associated with martingale representations. Finite-dimensional noise truncations and Yosida approximations are employed to establish approximate and asymptotic approximate completeness results. We introduce geometric Brownian motions in Hilbert spaces and derive sufficient conditions for the existence and uniqueness of an equivalent risk-neutral measure, together with explicit pricing formulas for some tractable examples. These results extend key aspects of the classical Black--Scholes framework to markets with infinite-dimensional asset-price dynamics. As a concrete application, the model can be interpreted as a segmented market consisting of a sequence of one-dimensional geometric Brownian motions.
item.dc:creator: Hanchao Liu

item.title: Certifiably Correct Fr\'echet Means in Orbit Spaaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.24191v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study Fr\'echet means in orbit spaces of finite orthogonal group actions. Since computing these means is NP-hard in general, we take inspiration from group synchronization to develop tractable spectral and semidefinite relaxations. Pairwise alignment certifies global optimality and we develop a semidefinite certificate that can extend beyond this condition. For Gaussian data modulo sign, we prove that our certificate succeeds in a high-noise regime where alignment fails. Numerical experiments evaluate these methods in various settings, including summarizing ensembles of districting plans and clustering time series
item.dc:creator: Dustin G. Mixon, Tom Needham, Nathan Willey

item.title: Diamond Maximal Operators: Classification, Moduli, and Oscillation Envelopes
item.description: arXiv:2610.24201v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study maximal averages generated by bounded cancellative kernels taking values in finite-dimensional real normed spaces, on Euclidean balls and on balls in a non-Archimedean local field with a fixed uniformizer. For angular kernels, pointwise domination of the full maximal operators is equivalent to factorization of their angular averaging maps, with the same optimal constant. Nonzero scalar angular comparison classes are therefore projective kernel classes. For angular kernels constant on a fixed finite measurable partition of the direction space, symmetric convex bodies classify exact norm measurements, Grassmannians parametrize nonzero classes under mutual domination, and positive semidefinite Gram matrices classify Hilbert-valued measurements. For general kernels, the closed convex hull of the averaging densities obtained from all scales and the dual unit ball is a complete invariant of the full maximal operator. A dilation example exhibits identifications of residue kernels beyond scaling and unit-coordinate changes. For nonzero radial residue kernels on bounded inputs, mutual domination is classified by the unit-circle zeros of filter polynomials, counted with multiplicity, with optimal constants given by the $\ell^1$ norms of convolution quotients. We identify the envelope over all normalized bounded cancellative kernels with the best local $L^1$ approximation by constants and prove quantitative convergence of residue envelopes as the resolution increases. Finally, the weights of the finite Fourier transform classify the one-level energy and the associated Carleson functional. This functional is equivalent to the $BMO_2$ seminorm precisely when every nontrivial additive character of the residue field is detected, and the weights determine the optimal comparison constants.
item.dc:creator: Mohammadreza Mohajer

item.title: Certified neural approximations for parabolic obstacle problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.24202v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Residual-trained neural surrogates carry no error guarantee, a limitation for free-boundary problems such as phase change and contact. We derive guaranteed error bounds for neural approximations of parabolic obstacle problems in first-order state--flux--multiplier form. The main result bounds the flux error of the network and the energy error of its feasible projection $\max\{v,g\}$ by the constitutive residual, the initial mismatch, the complementarity defect, and the PDE residual weighted by $c_F^2/\alpha$, without the coercivity and norm-equivalence constants of the first-order formulation. It extends the Apushkinskaya--Repin majorant for the heat operator to general coefficients, free multipliers and a flux bound. A penetration-consistency result shows that neural triples with arbitrarily small bound exist. Outward-rounded cellwise Taylor-model enclosures turn the bound into a finite computation valid on any adaptive partition. The flux and gradient errors of the projected output are certified below $0.27$ and $0.33$ of the solution scale for a one-dimensional Stefan problem and, after adaptive refinement, below one half for all three trained networks on a two-dimensional expanding disk. On an expanding ellipse the gradient bound stays above one half; substitution diagnostics trace the floor of the trained networks to the projected state near the free boundary, and the remaining gap to enclosure overhead. Without a closed-form solution, a validated lower bound replaces the solution norm; there the enclosure is nearly exact, but the trained networks have errors above the solution scale and no useful accuracy is certified. The bounds control a state--flux norm, not the multiplier or the free-boundary location.
item.dc:creator: Davood Damircheli

item.title: Constructive Universal Approximation by Infinite-Dimensional Neural Networks via Gaussian-Weighted Ridgelet Transform
item.description: arXiv:2610.24293v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neural networks whose inputs are functions, as in operator learning, are usually shown to be universal by existence arguments, either by reduction to finite-dimensional networks or by Stone--Weierstrass-type density; these prove that approximants exist but say little about how the parameters depend on the target. We take a constructive route. We extend the ridgelet transform, an integral transform related to the Fourier, Radon, and wavelet transforms, to continuous maps on a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space, replacing the Lebesgue measure that is unavailable in infinite dimensions by Gaussian weights with a homogeneous mixture on the direction space. The resulting transform has a Plancherel identity and reconstruction formulas incorporating the frame operator, the correction induced by the weights, and it assigns to each target an explicit coefficient measure, one for every admissible analysis filter. From these representations we obtain uniform approximation on compact sets for all continuous non-polynomial activations of polynomial growth, including ReLU, and, by Monte Carlo sampling of the coefficient, finite-width networks with a dimension-free $O(N^{-1/2})$ error in the width $N$ for globally Lipschitz activations and coefficients with finite variation and second moments. Explicit examples include Gaussian targets and neural-operator layers. A companion Lean~4 formalization provides machine-checked proofs, with its correspondence to the manuscript documented at https://shosonoda.github.io/lean-operator-ridgelet/ .
item.dc:creator: Sho Sonoda, Luca Galimberti, Yuanchao Xu, Isao Ishikawa, Masahiro Ikeda

item.title: The Casimir on the $K$-fixed tensor square of the minimal representation of $G_{2(2)}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.24656v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute the quadratic Casimir on the $K$-fixed subspace of the Hilbert tensor square of the unitary minimal representation of the split real group $G_{2(2)}$. In an explicit algebraic basis of invariant tensors, the Casimir acts by a three-term recurrence. Normalizing this basis yields a symmetric Jacobi operator whose self-adjoint realization is unitarily equivalent to multiplication by $-\frac92-8x^2$ in a Wilson-polynomial model with parameters $(\frac34,\frac34,\frac7{12},\frac{11}{12})$. We give the normalized spectral density and the unitary transform. The resulting spectrum is purely absolutely continuous, equals $(-\infty,-\frac92]$, and has scalar spectral multiplicity one.
item.dc:creator: Hongrui Yuan

item.title: Sharp Capacity Estimates and Volume Growth for Fractional Sobolev Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.24752v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We obtain sharp two-sided estimates for the relative capacity of fat and thin annuli in the fractional Sobolev spaces $W^s_{p,q}$, where $s\in(0,1)$, $p\in(0,\infty)$, $q\in(0,\infty]$, in terms of an explicit volume growth quantity. The underlying space is a general metric measure space equipped with a doubling and reverse doubling measure. In particular, whenever the capacity is finite, the estimates are independent of the parameter $q$. For $p<q$, we also introduce a sharp condition on the underlying measure that is necessary for the existence of admissible functions in $W^s_{p,q}$ space.
item.dc:creator: Angha Agarwal

item.title: Calder\'on Commutators on Quantum Euclidean Spaces and Quantum Tori
item.description: arXiv:2610.24881v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the classical setting, Calder\'on's first commutator theorem states that Lipschitz regularity of the symbol characterizes the $L_2$-boundedness of the first commutators. We show that the formally analogous assertion fails on every quantum Euclidean space $\R^d_\theta$ with $\theta\neq 0$. The same simultaneous failure occurs on $\T_\theta^d$ whenever $\theta$ has an irrational entry. For rational $\theta$, we obtain the optimal logarithmic bound for the corresponding Calder\'on first commutator. We also discuss the connection between Calder\'on's first commutator and the $T1$ theorem, and construct an operator-valued counterexample to Calder\'on's first commutator theorem, which shows that there is no direct analogue of the classical $T1$ theorem in the operator-valued setting. The counterexamples and the optimality argument rely on the construction of sequences of matrices $\mathsf D_n$ and $\mathsf A_n$ such that $\|[\mathsf D_n,\mathsf A_n]\|$ is uniformly bounded, whereas $\|[|\mathsf D_n|,\mathsf A_n]\|$ tends to infinity. This phenomenon reflects the failure of the absolute value function to be operator Lipschitz with respect to the operator norm. The logarithmic estimate, on the other hand, is obtained by combining matrix-valued $T1$ theory with a transference argument.
item.dc:creator: Deyu Chen, Guixiang Hong

item.title: On the isoperimetric profile in infinite dimensional pro-Lie groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.25088v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $K$ be a nontrivial compact connected Lie group with a bi-invariant Riemannian metric. On the compact pro-Lie group $K^{\N}$ we define a weighted variation by summing the distributional variations in its Lie group coordinates. We prove that all sublevel sets with bounded $L^1$-norm and weighted variation are compact in $L^1$ if and only if the coordinate weights tend to infinity. The proof gives a quantitative estimate for approximation by Haar averages over normal subgroups, illustrating that it is possible to apply a methodology which is typical of the geometric measure theory in a specific area of the topological group theory. The resulting perimeter is invariant under left and right translations and is preserved under pullback by quotient homomorphisms equipped with quotient metrics. Isoperimetric minimizers exist at every prescribed Haar probability. For the infinite torus, the compactness condition is equivalent to properness of a weighted length on its character group and to compactness of a Fourier multiplier's resolvent. Finally, we show that locally compact noncompact groups require an additional condition of tightness, in order to be treated as an appropriate generalization of the compact case.
item.dc:creator: Eniola Kazeem (FUTA), Francesco G. Russo (UNICAM)

item.title: Sharp quantum logarithmic Sobolev inequalities via semigroup interpolation
item.description: arXiv:2610.25180v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a semigroup interpolation method for sharp logarithmic Sobolev inequalities using spectral calculus and estimates of $\mathrm{Re}\langle\,Lx,x^2\rangle_2$, where $L$ generates an auxiliary symmetric quantum Markov semigroup. We apply the method to free groups and to crossed products of a finite von Neumann algebra $\mathcal N$ by $\mathbb Z$ or $\mathbb Z_n$, for $n=2$ or $n\ge4$, when the action commutes with the semigroup on $\mathcal N$. In particular, the word-length generators on quantum tori and the Weyl word-length generators on $M_n(\mathbb C)$ satisfy logarithmic Sobolev inequalities with optimal constant $2$.
item.dc:creator: Gan Yao

item.title: Exact probability laws of random inner products: Dirichlet splines, overlaps, uncertainty, and Bargmann invariants
item.description: arXiv:2610.25196v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Inner products of random matrices and random quantum states---such as orbital inner products, expectation values, overlaps, and cyclic Bargmann invariants---are shown to follow from two underlying mechanisms: the diagonal of an induced random state is Dirichlet distributed, and the expectation value of a random pure state in a rank-one or two-by-two operator is a numerical shadow on an elliptical disk. For states induced by an environment of dimension $K$, the expectation value of any observable is a Curry--Schoenberg spline with each eigenvalue repeated $K$ times, and the vector of moments has an explicit density on a simplex; for a qutrit, the variance law is obtained in finite form. The overlap of two random qubit states attains its mode at its mean for every rotation-invariant ensemble, but for Hilbert--Schmidt qutrits the density at the mean has a strictly negative derivative, so mode and mean separate; for large environments, the centred overlap converges to a variance-gamma law rather than a Gaussian. For two noncommuting qubit observables, the joint law of the two standard deviations is derived for all $K$, and the probability of coming within a small distance of the optimal sum of variances scales as a power of that distance, with a different exponent when the Bloch axes are orthogonal. For three Haar-random qubit states, the exact density of the Bargmann invariant is given in terms of a complete elliptic integral, together with its local behaviour and elementary marginals. In every dimension, the probability that its real part is negative---certifying basis-independent coherence---is computed, along with all mixed moments. For cycles of arbitrary length, the invariant is shown to be driven by an exact three-parameter Markov chain, and the logarithm of its modulus obeys a law of large numbers and a central limit theorem.
item.dc:creator: Lin Zhang

item.title: Noncommutative $L_p$-Poincar\'{e} inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2610.25277v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We derive $L_p$-Poincar\'{e} inequalities for quantum Markov semigroups on finite von Neumann algebras, from a spectral gap (PI) or from a modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality (MLSI). For $p\ge2$, the corresponding coefficients have optimal order $O(p)$ and $O(\sqrt p)$, respectively. Both estimates follow from Beckner inequalities by integration along semigroups. We also establish a non-tracial extension to quantum Markov semigroups satisfying GNS detailed balance. As a direct byproduct, we apply $L_p$-Poincar\'{e} inequalities to Schatten-valued functions on graphs in order to obtain the Schatten distortion of expanders.
item.dc:creator: Li Gao, Marius Junge, Zhendong Xu, Hao Zhang

item.title: A dual variational principle for the Moser-Trudinger inequality: existence, uniqueness and stability of extremals
item.description: arXiv:2610.25375v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For $p>1$, with $p'=p/(p-1)$, we prove the sharp dual inequality $$ \int_0^1-\log\left(1-\frac{\left|\int_0^xf(y) dy\right|^{p'}}{x}\right) dx\leq\mathsf{K}_p, \qquad \|f\|_{L^p(0,1)}\leq1, $$ where $\mathsf{K}_p$ is the logarithm of the optimal value in Moser's one-dimensional formulation of the Moser-Trudinger inequality. The dual functional follows from the Gibbs variational principle, monotone transport and the Legendre transform. Its supremum is attained, giving a dual proof of the existence theorems of Carleson-Chang (1986) and Hudson-Leckband (2002); the classical concentration threshold is realized by equality cases in Hoelder's inequality. For $p=2$ we prove, with rigorous computer-assisted estimates, that the nonnegative dual maximizer is unique and nondegenerate. Hence the extremal of the Moser-Trudinger inequality on a disk $D$ is unique up to sign, confirming conjectures of Adimurthi-Karthik-Giacomoni (2016) and of Chen-Lu-Xue-Zhu (2026). The positive extremal $u_*$ is nondegenerate, and, writing $\mathcal{M}_D(u)=|D|^{-1}\int_De^{4\pi u^2} dx$, we obtain $$ \mathcal{M}_D(u_*)-\mathcal{M}_D(u) \geq c \min_{\pm}\|\nabla(u\mp u_*)\|_{L^2(D)}^2 $$ for all $u\in H_0^1(D)$ with $\|\nabla u\|_{L^2(D)}\leq1$. Here $c>0$, and the exponent two is optimal, giving a quantitative stability theorem of Bianchi-Egnell type.
item.dc:creator: Jungang Li, Wen Sun

item.title: Cutoff beyond non-negative curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.26019v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study how a relaxed gradient estimate is enough to prove cutoff for several new families of Markov processes, within the varentropy framework of [Sal25]. In particular, we show how certain regularization estimates from hypocoercivity theory allow one to prove cutoff for kinetic dynamics. Moreover, we prove cutoff for some families of diffusions with non-convex potentials and for mean-field dynamics, as well as for biased random walks on the symmetric group, giving a simple proof of a far-reaching extension of a result of [NY24].
item.dc:creator: Max Fathi, Arnaud Guillin, Cyril Labb\'e, Justin Salez

item.title: Singular Stability Estimates for Passive Gamma Emission Tomography of Spent Nuclear Fuel
item.description: arXiv:2610.26276v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the joint recovery of attenuation and source coefficients from the attenuated X-ray transform, motivated by passive gamma emission tomography of spent nuclear fuel. Both coefficients are constant on known, disjoint disks of equal radius representing fuel rods. The surrounding moderator has known attenuation and zero source. We use tangential singularities of the data to give a sufficient condition on the geometry and coefficients for unique joint reconstruction from full data. For rods arranged on parallel rows separated by more than one rod diameter, with source coefficients uniformly bounded away from zero, we derive explicit reconstruction formulas and stability estimates for both coefficients. The estimates use a singular seminorm determined by two functionals per rod, computed from angular data near selected tangencies. Numerical experiments examine the approximation of these functionals from discretized data.
item.dc:creator: Tommi Heikkil\"a, Tapio Helin, Sean Holman, Shubham R. Jathar, Jesse Railo

item.title: Invertible non-cyclic functions in the little Bloch space
item.description: arXiv:2610.26318v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper presents a method for exhibiting functions $F$ in the little Bloch space $\B_0$ which are invertible, in the sense that $1/F$ also belongs to $\B_0$, and yet fail to be cyclic for the forward shift. The functions obtained in this way give rise to shift-invariant subspaces in $\B_0$ of index two, of a special type. The approach rests on a harmonic-measure criterion for non-cyclicity. This criterion gives a new manifestation of a principle of Borichev and Hedenmalm, and applies in a broad class of spaces of analytic functions.
item.dc:creator: Adem Limani

item.title: A direct obstacle proof of a dimension-free weak-type $(1,1)$ bound for the Gaussian Riesz transforms
item.description: arXiv:2610.26478v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a detailed, direct proof of a dimension-free weak-type $(1,1)$ estimate for the first-order Gaussian vector Riesz transform, using the fractional obstacle method of Ouyang, Spector, and Stockdale. For $d\gamma_n=\pi^{-n/2}e^{-|x|^2}\,dx$, let $L=-\tfrac12\Delta+x\cdot\nabla$, $D=2^{-1/2}\nabla$, and $R_\gamma=DL^{-1/2}\Pi_0$, where $\Pi_0$ removes the mean. We prove that $R_\gamma$ has weak-type constant at most $2$ on real-valued inputs, independently of $n$. The main construction is the unique unshifted decomposition $F=g+L^{1/2}u$, for nonnegative $F\in L^2(\gamma_n)$ and $a>\int F\,d\gamma_n$, with $u\geq0$, $\min\{F,a\}\leq g\leq a$, preservation of mass, and $g=a$ on $\{u>0\}$. We retain the details of coercivity, the Lewy--Stampacchia estimate, the upgrade from the form domain to the operator domain, and locality. We also identify the $L^1$ extension with the principal-value transform and obtain the constant $8/\pi$ for complex-valued inputs.
item.dc:creator: Cristian E. Guti\'errez, Juan Manfredi

item.title: Commutative Counterexamples to Arveson's Hyperrigidity Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.26556v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct counterexamples to Arveson's hyperrigidity conjecture for operator systems in commutative $C^*$-algebras. In each example, every irreducible representation of the $C^*$-envelope is a boundary representation, but hyperrigidity fails. The first example is the operator system of continuous affine functions on an infinite-dimensional weighted $\ell^p$ ball. In the second infinite-dimensional example, we start with commuting operators and construct a nontrivial dilation. The final example comes from a compact truncated epigraph of a strictly convex function and yields a finite-dimensional operator system.
item.dc:creator: Boris Bilich, Marcel Scherer

item.title: An example of a reflexive Banach space with an uncomplemented isometric subspace
item.description: arXiv:2309.15261v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present an example of a reflexive Banach space $X$ with a basis $(e_i)_{i=1}^\infty$ 1-equivalent to its subsequence $(e_{2i})_{i=1}^\infty$. The closed subspace of $X$ spanned by the latter is not complemented in $X$, whereas the subsequence $(e_{2i-1})_{i=1}^\infty$ is unconditional.
item.dc:creator: Anna Pelczar-Barwacz

item.title: Geometric conditions which imply $w^*$-normal structure
item.description: arXiv:2504.09464v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X$ be a complex Banach space. In their seminal work, Lau and Mah (\cite{LM}) study a geometric property called Lim's condition which, for separable $X$, implies that for any non-empty $w^*$-compact convex set $K \subset X^*$, any nonexpansive mapping $T: K \rightarrow K$ has a fixed point. In this paper, we study a weaker form of Lim's condition, which we call weak-Lim's condition. We prove that if $\ell_1 \not\hookrightarrow X$, then weak-Lim's condition on $X^*$ implies the fixed point property for non-expansive maps on weakly compact subsets of $X$. In the case of a commutative $C^\ast$-algebra, we prove that weak-Lim's condition is equivalent to Lim's condition. We show that Lim's condition characterizes $C^*$-algebras which are a $c_0$-direct sum of finite-dimensional operator spaces, while weak-Lim's condition characterizes $C^*$-algebras which are a $c_0$-direct sum of the spaces of compact operators on Hilbert spaces. For a uniform algebra, we extend a result of Lau and Mah to show that weak-Lim's condition implies that the space is finite-dimensional. In the case of an $L^1$-predual space, we show that this condition implies $k$-smoothness of the norm in the sense considered in \cite{LR}.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal of Fixed Point Theory and Applications (2026)
item.dc:creator: Deepak Gothwal, T. S. S. R. K. Rao

item.title: Pseudo- Riesz Bases
item.description: arXiv:2510.18993v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We recently introduced the concept of pseudo-Riesz bases, extending the influential idea of near-Riesz bases first proposed by J. Holub in the 1990s. We established that pseudo-Riesz bases can be characterized as sequences with a Fredholm synthesis operator. Unlike Riesz bases, they are neither spanning nor independent, yet they retain valuable expansion properties. Relative and square-summable perturbation theorems provide stability results for these classes. For pseudo-Riesz systems of distinct real exponentials, the Hru$\check{s}\check{c}$ev, Nikol'ski$\breve{i}$ model and Toeplitz index theory yield a precise correction rule: positive index $p$ allows deletion of any $p$ original terms, negative index $-q$ allows adjunction of any $q$ distinct new real-frequency exponentials, and index zero characterizes Riesz bases. Thus optimal finite corrections can always be performed within the exponential family. As a consequence, we obtain an asymptotic form of Kadec's $\frac{1}{4}$-theorem that permits finitely many arbitrary frequency deviations, provided distinctness is preserved.
item.dc:creator: Deborpita Biswas, Mishko Mitkovski

item.title: Weak and Strong Convergence of an Implicit Iteration for Hemi-Contractive Semigroups in Banach Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2606.25799v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study an implicit iteration for approximating common fixed points of strongly continuous semigroups on closed convex subsets of real Banach spaces. Under a stepwise Lipschitz restriction and hemi-contractivity relative to the common fixed point set, we establish well-definedness and Fej% \'{e}r monotonicity of the iteration. In reflexive Banach spaces satisfying Opial's condition, we obtain a sufficient condition for weak convergence based on a normalized residual estimate, uniform continuity at zero along the generated sequence, and demiclosedness at fixed positive times. In general real Banach spaces, we prove strong convergence under a time-dependent directional contraction condition and a divergence condition coupling the iteration weights with the contraction strength. A linear example shows that vanishing time steps and a divergent sum of iteration weights alone do not ensure convergence to a common fixed point. A nonlinear planar evolution semigroup illustrates the applicability of the strong convergence theorem beyond the nonexpansive class.
item.dc:creator: Ferit G\"urb\"uz

item.title: The Cauchy dual subnormality problem in two variables
item.description: arXiv:2607.04420v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Cauchy dual subnormality problem asks whether the Cauchy dual of a $2$-isometry is subnormal. This problem has attracted considerable attention due to its connections with moment theory, operator theory, and complex function theory. In particular, it has been closely related to operator-theoretic models on function spaces such as de Branges--Rovnyak spaces and Dirichlet-type spaces. In this paper, we investigate the Cauchy dual subnormality problem in the multivariable setting of toral $2$-isometries. We show that if $\mathbf{T} = (T_1, T_2)$ is an analytic left-inverse commuting pair of toral $2$-isometries satisfying the joint kernel condition, then it is unitarily equivalent to an operator-valued weighted shift with invertible weights $\{W_{I}^{(j)}:j=1,2,I\in \mathbb{Z}_{+}^2\},$ where the initial weights $W_{0,0}^{(1)}$ and $W_{0,0}^{(2)}$ are positive operators. Moreover, if these initial weights commute, then the Cauchy dual $\mathbf{T}' := (T_1', T_2')$ is subnormal. We also construct an example in which the initial weights do not commute, and the corresponding Cauchy dual tuple $\mathbf{T'}=(T_1',T_2')$ fails to be subnormal. Finally, we establish a complete set of unitary invariants for pure toral $2$-isometries.
item.dc:creator: Soumyadip Dey

item.title: Quaternionic Quantum q-Oscillator and Unbounded Subnormal Operators
item.description: arXiv:2608.06032v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this note, we observe that the class of unbounded subnormal operators on quaternionic Hilbert spaces is a solution of quaternionic q-oscillator problem whose complex case is addressed by Szefraniec in [27]. We also address the connection of unbounded subnormal operators on quaternionic Hilbert spaces, quaternionic quantum harmonic q-oscillator and quaternionic quantum Economics using model theory of unbounded subnormal operators. Moreover, we study model theory for sub-2-normal operators on quaternionic Hilbert space.
item.dc:creator: T. Prasad, K Krishnan, E. Shine Lal

item.title: Commutators of a class of $\Psi$-bounded oscillation operators on abstract weighted Orlicz-Morrey spaces endowed with ball-basis and applications
item.description: arXiv:2608.25517v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In our previous work \cite{SZ2026}, we established a class of abstract Orlicz-Morrey spaces endowed with a ball-basis and introduced the notion of \(\Psi\)-bounded oscillation operators. The present paper further develops this theory by investigating sparse domination and weighted estimates for such operators and their commutators within the framework of abstract Orlicz-Morrey spaces endowed with a ball-basis. We obtain pointwise sparse domination results for the operators and establish their boundedness on weighted Orlicz-Morrey spaces. The hypotheses of these conclusions differ from those in the classical Orlicz-Morrey setting and do not rely on dyadic decompositions of Euclidean structure. Moreover, we study the duality of these spaces and prove that the dual of the associated block space is exactly the Orlicz-Morrey space under consideration.
item.dc:creator: Fate Shan, Wei Wang, Yuchen Li, Jiang Zhou

item.title: Separable quotients of pointwise function spaces and relative consistency
item.description: arXiv:2609.19351v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Assuming Jensen's diamond principle, we construct a separable crowded compact zero-dimensional space $K$ of weight $\aleph_1$ and cardinality $2^{\aleph_1}$ such that $C_p(K)$ has no infinite-dimensional Hausdorff separable linear quotient. In particular, $K$ is an Efimov space: it contains neither a nontrivial convergent sequence nor a copy of $\beta\mathbb N$. We also prove in ZFC that the existence of a separable quotient of this kind is equivalent to the existence of a metrisable one. On the positive side, established finite-support random-sign methods give a split quotient of $C_p(K)$ onto $(c_0)_p$ whenever $K$ is infinite compact and $w(K)<\operatorname{cov}\mathcal N$, with explicit norm-one operators. Consequently, the universal quotient assertion for compacta of weight $\aleph_1$ is independent relative to the consistency of ZFC alone. A real-valued measurable continuum gives the positive result below the continuum and reduces the remaining problem to separable compacta of weight exactly the continuum. The counterexample uses direct diamond prediction, a simultaneous successor lemma, and a compactness argument converting localised measure limits into differences of point masses.
item.dc:creator: Tomasz Kania, Jerzy K\k{a}kol

item.title: The strong reproducing kernel thesis for Hankel operators and the Garsia norm
item.description: arXiv:2609.33242v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a reproducing kernel Hilbert space $\mathcal H$ and a bounded operator $T$ on $\mathcal H$, we say that $T$ obeys the strong reproducing kernel thesis (SRKT) if $\|T\|=\sup_k\|Tk\|$, where $k$ ranges over the normalized reproducing kernels in $\mathcal H$. Two problems are posed. One of these is to determine which Hankel operators on the Hardy space $H^2$ obey the SRKT. The other concerns the geometry of the unit ball of $BMO$ with respect to the Garsia norm.
item.dc:creator: Konstantin M. Dyakonov

item.title: A relaxation to the post-composition approach to metric-valued Sobolev maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.04435v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish that the definition of Sobolev mappings from metric measure spaces to metric spaces relying on the post-composition approach of Ambrosio-Reshetnyak admits, under certain transparent assumptions on the spaces, an equivalent reformulation that is substantially weaker than the principal version. In detail, the corresponding definition requires maps of this kind to meet two successive tests in order to be called Sobolev: first a ''qualitative'' one and then a ''quantitative'' one. At the same time, our result allows the relevant conclusion to be drawn based solely on the ''qualitative'' part. Remarkably, the conditions on the spaces sufficient for this to hold fit entirely into the singular flavor of the subject. More explicitly, such a phenomenon emerges if either the source space is of finite Hausdorff dimension and satisfies the Sobolev-to-Luzin-Lipschitz property or the target space is of finite Hausdorff dimension. All this provides a significant generalization of several earlier achievements on the topic.
item.dc:creator: Roman D. Oleinik

item.title: Classification of bipartite observables I: stable and uniformly stable observables
item.description: arXiv:2610.11002v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This is the first of a series of three papers that bring model theory to quantum information. The dividing lines of Shelah's classification theory, which separate the tame first-order theories from the wild ones, become properties of bipartite observables: properties of the expectation values obtained when two independently prepared quantum systems are idealized one after the other. In this paper we focus on stability. An observable is stable when the order in which the two systems are idealized never changes its expectation value, and this is Shelah's stability. Its classical characterizations, in model theory and in analysis, acquire a physical meaning: idealized preparations are simulated by finite mixtures of actual ones, and adaptive probes can tell apart only polynomially many preparations.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Due\~nez, Jos\'e Iovino

item.title: Weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for noncommutative rough singular integrals
item.description: arXiv:2610.15633v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish the weak type \((1,1)\) endpoint estimate for operator-valued rough singular integrals with kernels satisfying the classical \(L\log L\) integrability and cancellation conditions. This extends Seeger's endpoint theorem [{J. Amer. Math. Soc.} \textbf{9} (1996)] to the noncommutative setting. A key ingredient is an off-diagonal analysis that controls interactions between different kernel scales and avoids an additional logarithmic loss.
item.dc:creator: Junming Cao, Wei Li, Lian Wu

item.title: Completely symmetric subspaces of noncommutative $L_p$-spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.18041v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $2<p<\infty$. We prove that every infinite-dimensional closed subspace $F$ of a noncommutative $L_p$-space contains a subspace completely isomorphic to $\ell_p$, $C_p$, $R_p$, or $C_p\cap R_p$ and completely complemented in $F$. This answers the question of Junge and Xu on the existence of completely symmetric basic sequences.
item.dc:creator: Jinghao Huang

item.title: Stable topology and stable compactness
item.description: arXiv:2610.22185v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: To solve a large class of noncompact problems ubiquitous in random functional analysis and its applications, most of compactness-based fundamental theorems established for normed spaces or locally convex spaces are required to be extended for random normed modules and random locally convex modules in an appropriate way of weakening compactness. To achieve this goal, in this paper we first develop stable set theory by introducing some new set-theoretic tools, then propose a class of topological spaces with a stable structure, called stable topological spaces, and in particular propose and systematically develop the theory of stably compact spaces, which is a natural generalization of that of compact spaces. The resulting theory is of independent interest from the perspective of general topology since its investigation requires an analysis of stratification structures coordinated with partitions of unity in a complete Boolean algebra. Finally, we show the power of the theory of stable compactness by establishing random Banach-Alaoglu, random James and random Banach-Bourbaki-Kakutani-\v{S}mulian theorems.
item.dc:creator: Tiexin Guo, Xiaohuan Mu, Pasqualetto Enrico, Qiang Tu, Guang Yang

item.title: Asymptotics of Constrained Quantization for Compactly Supported Measures
item.description:
arXiv:2505.10801v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study constrained quantization of a compactly supported probability $P$ on $\mathbb{R}^D$ by codebooks in a nonempty closed set $S$. For $0<r\le\infty$, the constrained error $e_{n,r}$ is attained and satisfies $e_{n,r}\downarrow L_r=\|\operatorname{dist}(\cdot,S)\|_{L^r(P)}$. Set $\Delta_{n,r}=e_{n,r}^r-L_r^r$ for finite $r$. A Borel nearest-point selector $T$ induces $\mu=T_*P$. Writing $q_{n,s}$ for the classical $L^s$ quantization error, we obtain $e_{n,r}-L_r\le2q_{n,r}(\mu)$ and $\Delta_{n,r}\le C_rq_{n,1}(\mu)$ for $1\le r<\infty$, with $C_r$ independent of $n$, and $\Delta_{n,r}\le2^rq_{n,r}(\mu)^r$ for $0<r<1$. Also, $e_{n,\infty}-L_\infty\le2c_n(E)$, where $E$ is the nearest-point image of $\operatorname{supp}P$ and $c_n(E)$ is its covering radius. For $1\le r<\infty$, a weighted power-growth condition with exponent $ eta>0$ on a fixed source set $F$ bounds $\Delta_{n,r}$ below by the classical $ eta$-power quantization cost of $
u_F=T_*(wP|_F)$. If $d
u_F=\widehat w\,d\eta$ for a compactly supported reference probability $\eta$ and $\widehat w\in A_p(\eta)$, $1<p<\infty$, then $\Delta_{n,r}\ge
u_F(\mathbb{R}^D)[\widehat w]_{A_p(\eta)}^{-1}q_{n, eta/p}(\eta)^ eta$. These comparisons yield bounds for the quantization dimensions defined by $e_{n,r}-L_r$ and $\Delta_{n,r}^{1/r}$, with distinct behavior at positive and zero baselines. Convex and uniformly prox-regular constraints supply the growth weights through their projection inequalities. Circle and lifted Cantor distributions give matching quadratic-excess rates, while rectifiable weighted projections give lower Zador estimates.
item.dc:creator: Chenxing Qian

item.title: Spectrum of the wave equation with Dirac damping on a compact star graph
item.description: arXiv:2510.09829v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the wave equation with a distributional Dirac damping and Dirichlet boundary conditions on a compact interval. It is shown that the spectrum of the corresponding wave operator is fully determined by zeroes of an entire function. Consequently, a considerable change of spectral properties is shown for certain critical values of the damping parameter. We also derive a definitive criterion for the Riesz basis property of the root vectors for an arbitrary placement of a complex-valued Dirac damping. Finally, we consider a generalisation of the problem for compact star graphs and provide insight into the essence of the critical damping constant.
item.dc:creator: Mikul\'a\v{s} Ku\v{c}era

item.title: Twisted operator algebras of self-similar groupoid actions on arbitrary graphs
item.description: arXiv:2511.07906v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study self-similar groupoid actions on arbitrary directed graphs together with $\mathbb{T}$-valued twists that exhaust the second cohomology group of the associated Zappa-Sz\'ep product category. We define and analyse the associated universal, reduced, and essential $C^*$-algebras, along with their Toeplitz versions and core subalgebras. In fact, we develop our theory in the more general setting of $L^P$-operator algebras, where $P\subseteq [1,\infty]$ is any non-empty set of parameters. This includes $C^*$-algebras, $L^p$-operator algebras and symmetrised $L^{p,*}$-operator algebras for $p\in [1,\infty]$, as special cases. We use three complementary approaches: twisted inverse semigroups, twisted ample groupoids, and $C^*$-correspondences. We provide, in terms of the self-similar action, general characterisations of topological freeness, minimality, Hausdorffness, finite non-Hausdorffness, effectiveness, and local contractiveness for the associated ample groupoids. We generalise the classical Cuntz--Krieger Uniqueness and Coburn--Toeplitz Uniqueness Theorems for graph $C^*$-algebras to twisted $L^P$-operator algebras of self-similar groupoid actions. We characterise when the natural inclusions are Cartan, give checkable criteria for simplicity and pure infiniteness of the essential algebras, and discuss when the universal and reduced algebras coincide. We also provide conditions that ensure the singular ideals vanish. Using the groupoid model we show that for any $P\subseteq [1,\infty]$, the $L^P$-operator algebra of a contracting self-similar action is simple if and only if the corresponding Steinberg algebra is simple. Using the Toeplitz-Pimsner model, we prove that for the universal groupoid of any self-similar groupoid action on a row-finite graph, the singular $C^*$-algebraic ideal always vanishes.
item.dc:creator: B. K. Kwa\'sniewski, A. Mundey

item.title: Reasoning about Continuous-Variable Quantum Systems
item.description: arXiv:2607.23137v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Continuous-variable quantum computing (CVQC) is a computing paradigm in which measurements yield values over a continuous domain. CVQC is both a convenient computational framework for modeling physical quantum systems, and a good abstraction for hardware platforms based on quantum optics. Yet, the semantic foundations of CVQC remain underdeveloped. To address this gap, we develop a formal semantics for a core CV quantum programming language, and sound verification methods for program correctness. A main contribution of this work is to isolate a well-behaved quantitative predicate domain that achieves sufficient expressiveness to accommodate unbounded values as they arise in the infinite-dimensional, continuous setting. Specifically, we choose closed positive quadratic forms as semantic predicates, representing finite expectations, domains of finiteness, and infinite penalties in one ordered object. We validate our choice by establishing that our semantic predicates satisfy desirable closure properties including the definition of weakest preconditions. We validate our design with two case studies, including an example based on the celebrated GKP error-correcting code, for which we establish a second moment bound.
item.dc:creator: Tianshi Yu, Gilles Barthe, Minbo Gao, Mingsheng Ying, Li Zhou

item.title: Single commutators in $C^*$-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2609.14585v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal A$ be a simple unital $C^*$-algebra with real rank zero, nonempty tracial state space $\mathcal T(\mathcal A)$, and strict comparison of projections. We prove that every element $T$ in $\mathcal A$ with $\tau(T)=0$ for all $\tau\in\mathcal T(\mathcal A)$ is a single commutator if one of the following conditions holds: $(1)$ $\mathcal A$ has unique trace; $(2)$ $\mathcal A$ has stable rank one. We also prove that every nonscalar element in a simple unital purely infinite $C^*$-algebra is a single commutator. Applications include UHF algebras, irrational rotation algebras, and Cuntz algebras.
item.dc:creator: Lu Cui, Minghui Ma

item.title: Sharp Truncated Difference Estimates for Nonlocal Nonconvex Functionals Defined by Superlevel Sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.04259v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $N\in\mathbb N$ and $p\in[1,\infty)$. In this article, we consider a family $\{\Phi_{\lambda,p}^{\gamma}\}_{\lambda\in(0,\infty)}$ of nonlocal nonconvex functionals with a real parameter $\gamma$ and establish two truncated difference estimates bounded by these functionals with the sharp range of $\gamma$; that is, for any $\gamma\in(-\infty,-1]$, any $\lambda\in(0,\infty)$, any cube $Q\subset\mathbb R^N$, and any measurable function $g:Q\to\mathbb R$, \begin{align*} &\int_Q\int_Q\left[\frac{|g(x)-g(y)|-\lambda|x-y|^{1+\gamma/p}}{\ell(Q)^{1+\gamma/p}}\right]_+^p\,dx\,dy\\ &\quad\lesssim \lambda^p\mathop{\int_Q\int_Q}\limits_{\frac{|g(x)-g(y)|}{|x-y|^{1+\gamma/p}}>\lambda}\left[\frac{|x-y|}{\ell(Q)}\right]^{\gamma-N}\,dx\,dy=:\frac{\Phi_{\lambda,p}^{\gamma}(g;Q)}{\ell(Q)^{\gamma-N}}, \end{align*} where the implicit positive constant depends only on $N$, $p$, and $\gamma$. For $\gamma\in(0,\infty)$, the above estimate holds with the left-most integrand replaced by $\frac{\min\{|g(x)-g(y)|^p,\lambda^p|x-y|^{p+\gamma}\}}{\ell(Q)^{p+\gamma}}$. As applications, these estimates yield related nonlocal Poincar\'e inequalities with the sharp range of $\gamma$, and also recover the known $\Gamma$-liminf lower bounds and characterizations of Sobolev and BV spaces in terms of the liminf of the functionals $\{\Phi^\gamma_{\lambda,p}\}_{\lambda\in(0,\infty)}$ for all $\gamma\in\mathbb{R}\setminus(-1,0]$. We investigate further applications to compactness and variational problems as well as a new VMO criterion. Inspired by a recent work of R. L. Frank, we develop an elementary approach based on dyadic iteration of truncated differences along line segments, which allows us to treat the aforementioned problems in a unified way.
item.dc:creator: Feng Dai, Dachun Yang, Wen Yuan, Yirui Zhao

item.title: Classification of bipartite observables II: NIP observables and the Todorcevic trichotomy
item.description: arXiv:2610.12908v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This is the second of a series of three papers that bring model theory to quantum information. The dividing lines of Shelah's classification theory, which separate the tame first-order theories from the wild ones, become properties of bipartite observables: properties of the expectation values obtained when two independently prepared quantum systems are idealized one after the other. In this paper we focus on Shelah's independence property. An observable without it has idealized responses of the first Baire class, and Todor\v{c}evi\'c's trichotomy for Rosenthal compacta divides such observables into three classes, each containing a physical order. In the transverse-field Ising model, the spontaneous magnetization decides whether the family of magnetizations is stable or lies in the second class.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Due\~nez, Jos\'e Iovino

item.title: Operator space theory from the maximal viewpoint
item.description: arXiv:2610.21929v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We initiate a theory of ``operator spaces" (in other words subspaces of $C^*$-algebras) with an emphasis on the maximal tensor product. The natural morphisms become the maximally bounded maps instead of the completely bounded ones. With this new looking glass we first examine various issues : lifting and extension properties, local reflexivity, inner derivations, similarity problems.This first part is semi-expository while the second one focuses on the class of von Neumann algebras $M$ such that any completely bounded unital homomorphism on a $C^*$-algebra with values in $M$ is maximally bounded (or equivalently is similar to a $*$-homomorphism via a similarity belonging to $M$). We show that this holds if and only if $M$ is the direct sum of a finite von Neumann algebra and an injective one. This also characterizes the $M$'s such that all completely bounded derivations into $M$ are inner. Our main tool for this is a new characterization of injective von Neumann algebras.
item.dc:creator: Gilles Pisier, Jean Roydor
